item.title: Italy stun France 3-1 to hand Zidane first defeat as Les Bleus coach
item.description: Italy came from behind to beat France 3-1 in Milan and hand Zidane his first defeat since taking charge of Les Bleus. France were without Kylian Mbappe and Ousmane Dembele due to injury but Michael Olise pounced on a loose pass from Gianluigi Donnarumma to fire them ahead on 10 minutes. Francesco Pio Esposito steered in Nicolo Cambiaghi’s pass to bring Italy level before France twice hit the post through Bradley Barcola and Rayan Cherki. Sebastiano Esposito blazed a second-half penalty wide for Italy, but Roberto Mancini’s side did not rue that miss as Davide Frattesi powered home Federico Dimarco’s cut-back. Francesco Pio Esposito then doubled his tally for the night, succeeding where his older brother had failed by converting a penalty after Dayot Upamecano fouled substitute Antonio Vergara. Italy climbed above France at the top of Group A1 on head-to-head record. Both teams have 10 points going into the final round of games, with Belgium just one point adrift. Belgium host Italy on Sunday and France are at home to Turkey. Turkey slid to a fifth straight loss as they went down 2-1 to Belgium in Izmir. Arda Guler’s magnificent free-kick put Turkey ahead under new coach and former midfielder Sergen Yalcin, but Belgium struck twice in quick succession with goals from Kevin De Bruyne and Charles De Ketelaere to come away with victory. item.title: US Congress Steps Up Scrutiny Of Trump, Nvidia After Huang Exit
item.description: Key US lawmakers on Thursday called for clarity on what the Trump administration knew about Nvidia chief Jensen Huang’s extramarital affair with a woman suspected of spying for China, after the AI chip giant announced his departure. Huang, now Nvidia’s former CEO, had pushed for looser rules on sales of US chips to China — crucial in the AI race — and the controversy has reenergized advocates of a hard line on Beijing, days before Donald Trump travels to China. “Despite Jensen Huang’s resignation, Congress must demand answers from Mr Huang and others at Nvidia about how they may have put US national security at risk,” Senate Democratic leader Chuck Schumer said on social media. “The Trump administration must also answer for what it did once it learned about Mr Huang’s relationship with a suspected Chinese intelligence asset,” he added. Huang, a co-founder of the AI chip giant, on Sunday acknowledged an affair with Alice Huang, a former executive at Singapore-based data centre company Megaspeed. The two are not related. US intelligence suspects her of working for Beijing, which has strongly denied the allegations. ‘Obvious Threat’ According to The New York Times, Trump was informed of the suspicions last year, and Secretary of State Marco Rubio confirmed them to him in May. Trump said on Monday he knew “the FBI is looking into” the affair, adding that he expected Huang to be “in good shape.” He said Huang had told him he did not know the woman was a spy. U.S. President Donald Trump delivers remarks during a ceremony in honor of Veterans Day at Arlington National Cemetery on November 11, 2026 in Arlington, Virginia. (Photo by Kevin Dietsch / GETTY IMAGES NORTH AMERICA / Getty Images via AFP) | Kevin Dietsch / GETTY IMAGES NORTH AMERICA / Getty Images via AFP Huang was ultimately brought down by the scandal on Thursday, when the company’s board announced his departure, effective immediately. Lawmakers are also raising questions about Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick’s alleged reluctance to impose restrictions on exports of the chips to China. Three Republican House committee chairmen had already said they wanted to hear from Huang behind closed doors on November 18. Democrats, who will take control of both chambers of Congress in January after winning the midterm elections, have also said they intend to look more closely into the affair. The top Democrats on the Senate Finance and House Ways and Means committees told Lutnick in a letter on Thursday that they were investigating the administration’s “scheme to approve and tax” Nvidia chip exports to Chinese firms linked to Beijing’s government and military. They accuse Lutnick and Trump of ignoring the “obvious national security threat” posed by the ties between Huang and a suspected Chinese intelligence agent, even though they had reportedly been informed of them. item.title: Spain beat Czech Republic to retain perfect Nations League record
item.description: Alex Baena scored from the spot and Marc Pubill added another seconds from time as Spain beat ten-men Czech Republic 2-0 in the Nations League in Prague on Thursday. The win leaves Spain unbeaten in 44 competitive games in a row, including five wins in as many Nations League games this season. Spain, who already secured a quarter-final berth before travelling to Prague, will face England in Madrid on Sunday in their final Group A3 game. Baena scored on 39 minutes after a VAR check revealed Czech midfielder Lukas Ambros had handled the ball inside the box. The Atletico Madrid winger blasted his spot kick past Matej Kovar who touched the ball but failed to clear it. Czech captain Ladislav Krejci was sent off in the 69th minute after bringing down second-half substitute Roberto Fernandez on a counter-attack. It was a deja-vu for the Wolverhampton defender who also got a red card at the end of Spain’s 3-1 home win over the Czechs last month. Pubill, another substitute, beat Kovar with a low shot deep into stoppage time after the Czech back four left him alone facing the Eindhoven goalkeeper. Luis de la Fuentes missed Lamine Yamal, Dani Olmo, Rodri and Eric Garcia over injuries while Mikel Oyarzabal was sidelined with flu for the Prague game. Spain got off to a slow start on the chilly evening but never really let the hosts get close throughout the first half. They gradually stepped up their pressure, often confining the Czechs to their box and looking for chances. Fabian Ruiz hit the post with a curling right-footer three minutes from halftime, while Dean Huijsen’s header found Kovar’s arms. Yeremy Pino, replacing Yamal on the right flank, saw his goal overturned by VAR for offside just two minutes into the second half. The Czechs showed higher spirits after the break, but David Zima tipped the ball over the bar from close range on 50 minutes and Adam Hlozek’s glancing header landed on the top of the crossbar. The Czechs lost momentum after the red card, but Baena had two efforts cleared by Kovar who also denied Fernandez from close range. The hosts, led by de la Fuente’s long-time collaborator Santi Denia, have lost all their Nations League games this season. They are next travelling to Croatia for a game they need to win to stay in the top tier of the competititon for the next edition. item.title: Record-breaking Kane fires England into Nations League knockouts
item.description: Harry Kane celebrated his record-breaking 126th England appearance with a goal from the penalty spot as England beat Croatia 2-1 on Thursday to book a place in the Nations League quarter-finals. Slaven Bilic’s team were determined to avoid the embarrassment of their 7-0 mauling by England in Rijeka last month and looked much more solid from the kick-off. But goals from Morgan Rogers and captain Kane kept England second in their group, confirming their place in the Nations League last eight in March. Neither side got out of second gear in the opening stages of the match at Wembley. Elliot Anderson fired over in the 16th minute and Croatia’s Josip Misic flashed a shot wide midway through the first half. Chelsea forward Rogers broke the deadlock in the 24th minute in slightly fortuitous fashion following a neat move by the home side. Kane floated a ball to Jude Bellingham on the right of the penalty area and the Real Madrid man cushioned the ball first time across the area towards Rogers. Manchester City’s Josko Gvardiol had a chance to clear but got in a tangle and Chelsea’s Rogers poked the ball past goalkeeper Dominik Livakovic. England started to find some rhythm as they went in search of a second goal but failed to add to their tally before half-time. Thomas Tuchel’s men were again the more potent team at the beginning of the second period. But the visitors levelled against the run of play just before the hour mark after a glaring error by England defender Jarell Quansah, who misdirected a header from close range towards Jordan Pickford following a Croatia corner. The ball fell to Petar Sucic, who stabbed home. Minutes later England were back in front, with Bayer Leverkusen defender Quansah again at the heart of the action after his shirt was tugged in the penalty area. Referee Morten Krogh initially did not award a penalty but he was sent to the monitor by the VAR and pointed to the spot. Kane made no mistake, drilling home for record-extending 92nd England goal. Nikola Vlasic gave England a scare, firing just wide of Jordan Pickford’s goal as Croatia showed they were still alive. James Garner thought he had scored a third for England after a Bellingham cut-back but Bellingham was in an off-side position when he received the ball. Ballon d’Or winner Kane won his 126th cap when the game kicked off — taking him clear of his tie with former goalkeeper Peter Shilton. A giant banner was raised before kick-off with a picture of the 33-year-old and the words “England’s Finest”. Shilton was part of a pre-match presentation to honour the Three Lions skipper, along with Football Association patron Prince William. England remain second in Nations League Group A3, after leaders Spain beat the Czech Republic 2-0 but are now assured of a place in the quarter-finals. Spain and England face each other in Madrid on Sunday. The post Record-breaking Kane fires England into Nations League knockouts appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Online safety concerns are reshaping how people meet strangers
item.description: It’s hard to ignore how meeting new people online has changed in the past decade. With so many platforms connecting millions, the possibilities feel endless, but the risks have become more visible too. Stories about scams, harassment, and data breaches are everywhere, and they’ve made people think twice before reaching out to someone they don’t know. Safety concerns aren’t just in the background anymore—they’re shaping the way we start conversations, choose platforms, and decide how much to share. As awareness grows, so do new habits and expectations for digital introductions. This shift doesn’t just affect individuals; it’s influencing whole communities as we all adapt to a more cautious, connected world. Changing first steps: why some users now engage with strangers differently online That growing caution is easy to spot in the way people now approach first interactions with strangers online. Instead of jumping right into open conversations, many start by looking for platforms that let them control who they talk to, or give them the option to remain anonymous until they feel comfortable. Features like one-click exit buttons, video previews, or private chat rooms have become popular for exactly this reason. Women, in particular, are leading this change. They’re more likely to say safety is a top concern, which shows up in everything from avoiding certain apps to using aliases or insisting on in-app messaging only. The choice of platform matters too. Video chat sites, for example, offer a sense of control because users can see and hear who they’re talking to—and can leave the conversation instantly if something doesn’t feel right. For many, getting to know LuckyCrush and similar services is part of this shift toward safer, more controlled first steps when meeting someone new. It’s a sign that concerns are not stopping people from connecting, but are changing the rules for how those first moments happen. a shift in trust: navigating caution in the age of digital introductions That change in first steps is really about trust—how it’s built, how it’s lost, and why it matters so much now. People aren’t just jumping into conversations and sharing details the way they might have a decade ago. Instead, there’s this sense of needing to pause and check for warning signs. With more stories surfacing about online fraud and harassment, it feels riskier to let your guard down. A lot of users now watch for inconsistent stories, pressure to move chats off-platform, or requests for private information as red flags that something isn’t right. Some of the ways people protect themselves include sticking to messaging within the app, looking for verification badges, or even googling someone before agreeing to meet. These habits are becoming more common, especially as platforms roll out tools designed for safer interactions. The numbers back up this shift in attitude. item.title: UNN Deaths: Gov Mbah mourns, orders investigation
item.description: Governor of Enugu State, Dr Peter Mbah, has expressed deep grief over the deaths of four students of the University of Nigeria, Nsukka, UNN, who reportedly died during an off-campus sign-out party organised for one of their friends, describing the incident as a heartbreaking loss. Mbah described the deaths as a grievous loss, not only to the immediate families of the deceased and the university, but also to Enugu State as a whole. He called for a ban on sign-out parties among undergraduates, noting that the practice had brought too much sorrow to families and tertiary institutions across the country. This was contained in a press statement issued by the governor’s media aide, Mazi Uche Anichukwu, on Thursday. “I received with rude shock and deep sense of loss the news of the off-campus sign-out party leading to the death of four students of the University of Nigeria Nsukka, and hospitalisation of six others. “This is a grievous loss not only to the immediate families of the deceased and the university, but also to us as a state. Losing them in their prime and along with their promising future cuts as deeply as a sharp knife. We, therefore share in this grief and pray God to grant their families, friends, and the UNN community the equanimity to bear the heartbreaking loss. “Our hearts go out to their parents in particular, who sacrificed personal comforts to sponsor their children through the university, but only to face this sad turn of events. “As a government, we have ordered a thorough investigation into the circumstances surrounding their deaths and will work closely with the university authorities and security agencies to get to the roots of the sad development and forestall a recurrence. “In the meantime, I have suspended my scheduled town hall meeting with the UNN community on Friday, November 13, 2026, as we join the university in mourning the dead. “Going forward, we will work with the authorities of tertiary institutions to enforce a full ban on sign-out parties and other excessive celebrations, a trend that has cost more lives and brought more sorrows than joy to families and higher institutions of learning,” the governor stated. Mbah also called for increased public enlightenment campaigns by relevant agencies and institutions on the consequences of drug use and abuse. He prayed for the peaceful repose of the souls of the deceased. The post UNN Deaths: Gov Mbah mourns, orders investigation appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: ‘His Support Base Still Strong’, Doherty Says Obi Can Repeat 2023 Feat In Lagos
item.description: The Lagos governorship candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Funso Doherty, says the party’s presidential candidate, Peter Obi, retains a strong support base and has the backing to repeat his 2023 electoral performance in Lagos State. Doherty said this during an interview on Channels Television’s Politics Today on Thursday, following an attack on the party’s town hall meeting in Lagos. He dismissed suggestions that Obi’s reception among Nigerians could be weakened by his defection from the Labour Party to the NDC, arguing that his appeal is rooted in his political philosophy rather than the platform on which he contests elections. “The idea of a new party is not something that we should hang our hat on anymore in our clime. Parties may be new, but the individuals involved are not new. “But the reception of Peter Obi today, that is how it is everywhere he goes. This is a man who is loved by the people. They view him as a different kind of politician, for good reason, and those of us who align with that philosophy and thinking,” he said. Doherty warned against underestimating Obi’s political influence, saying such an assumption could prove costly. “Anybody who is making a contrary case, time will tell. But I would advise them that if they are saying that just to downplay his significance, I think it will be a grave mistake on their part because his support base is still strong. I have seen it, not just today, we have seen it multiple times,” he added. He said the resistance by NDC supporters to the disruption of the party’s town hall meeting was evidence that the enthusiasm which characterised Obi’s 2023 presidential campaign had not diminished. “Those guys came in today probably thinking they would have an easy ride of it. They would come in and do what they might normally do, scatter things and people would run away. But people were not in that frame of mind. “We have laboured for this, and you cannot deprive us of it. And I think that spirit is alive and strong. To those who might think that, following 2023, people have lost some of that energy, I think, if anything, today should let us know that it is game on.” Attack On NDC supporters An injured NDC supporter during the attack by suspected thugs in Lagos Doherty also condemned the attack on the party’s town hall meeting at Classic Event Place in Oregun, Ikeja, describing it as “unprovoked” and “unnecessary.” Suspected political thugs invaded the venue on Thursday ahead of the arrival of Obi and his supporters. The attackers, said to be armed with cutlasses, cudgels and stones, allegedly vandalised property and damaged several vehicles parked within the premises. However, NDC supporters resisted the attackers, confronting them and throwing chairs in an attempt to drive them away. The confrontation disrupted activities at the venue before security operatives intervened. item.title: My Ambition Is To Ensure Tinubu’s 2027 Victory, Says Matawalle
item.description: The Minister of State for Defence, Bello Matawalle, says his major ambition is to ensure the re-election of President Bola Tinubu in the 2027 general elections. Matawalle made this known while addressing supporters of the All Progressives Congress (APC) at his residence in Gusau, Zamfara State, ahead of the expected visit of the First Lady, Senator Remi Tinubu. He urged party members to unite and intensify mobilisation for Tinubu’s re-election, as well as the victory of other APC candidates in the state. The minister commended Tinubu’s efforts in tackling insecurity, developing infrastructure and promoting political cohesion, expressing his commitment to ensuring that the President completes his eight-year tenure. Matawalle said that after discharging his responsibilities as Minister of State for Defence, particularly in the fight against insecurity, his next major priority would be to work towards Tinubu’s re-election. He also dismissed what he described as provocations and propaganda by individuals seeking to tarnish his image, insisting that his priority was to sustain unity within the APC in Zamfara and secure victories for the party at all levels. The minister further dismissed allegations and propaganda concerning Tinubu’s health, maintaining that the President was fit to continue providing leadership and direction for the country. On security, Matawalle assured Zamfara residents that the Federal Government would deploy additional security personnel along major highways to protect commuters from persistent bandit attacks. He specifically mentioned the Talata Mafara-Gusau-Sokoto highway, as well as the Gummi-Anka-Bukkuyum and Tsafe access roads, as routes that would receive increased security attention. “We will deploy security forces along the Talata Mafara-Gusau-Sokoto highway to ensure the safe movement of commuters. We will also deploy security personnel to ensure the safety of those travelling along the Gummi, Anka, Bukkuyum and Tsafe roads,” he said. Matawalle pledged to do everything within his capacity to address insecurity in Zamfara and other parts of the country. He also spoke on the controversy surrounding the rerun election in Zamfara North Senatorial District, dismissing allegations of attempts to undermine his political standing and create divisions within the APC. The minister questioned the rationale behind the violence reportedly recorded during the rerun elections in Kaura Namoda and Birnin Magaji, insisting that political disagreements should not lead to attacks or destruction. “Those who caused the crisis during the rerun elections in Kaura Namoda and Birnin Magaji know whether they can emerge victorious or not. If victory is on your side, what is the essence of creating a crisis? We will not fight or attack anybody,” he said. item.title: 2027: ‘Arrest perpetrators’, Senate condemns political violence nationwide
item.description: By Henry Umoru AHEAD of 2027 Presidential and general elections, the Senate has condemned in very strong terms, cases of political violence, attacks and disruption of political activities across the country. The Senate has thus taken a swipe at acts of violence, intimidation, assault and destruction of property associated with political rallies, meetings, processions and other lawful political activities, irrespective of the political parties or individuals affected. The Senate has urged the security agents to as a matter of urgency apprehend whoever is culpable in such heinous act in order to serve as deterrent to others. The Upper Chamber has called on all political parties, candidates and their supporters to reject inflammatory rhetoric, discourage violence and cooperate with security agencies in maintaining public peace. Speaking with Vanguard yesterday, Chairman of the Senate Committee on Media and Public Affairs, Senator Yemi Adaramodu, APC, Ekiti South, said, “President Bola Ahmed Tinubu is preaching peace and national harmony, the National Assembly is in support of Mr President on this. “We thus condemn in totality any act of political violence and urge the security agents to apprehend whoever is culpable in such heinous act.” Vanguard News The post 2027: ‘Arrest perpetrators’, Senate condemns political violence nationwide appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: AFCONQ: Why I didn’t invite Maduka Okoye – Chelle
item.description: Super Eagles head coach Eric Chelle has explained his decision to leave goalkeeper Maduka Okoye out of Nigeria’s squad for their 2027 Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON) qualifying matches. Chelle, who is preparing the Super Eagles for their double-header against Tanzania, said his selection decisions were based on considerations both on and off the pitch. The Franco-Malian tactician insisted that the national team was not obligated to any particular player, stressing that his choices were guided by his assessment of what was best for the squad. “The national team is not close to him or anyone. I made my choice and when I made my choice I made it around the pitch and outside it,” Chelle said. Okoye, who plays for Italian club Udinese, has been absent from recent Super Eagles selections, with Stanley Nwabali, Francis Uzoho and Arthur Okonkwo among the goalkeepers considered by the coach. Chelle’s latest comments underline his position that selection for the national team is based on his technical and other considerations rather than a player’s reputation or status. The Super Eagles are seeking to strengthen their position in the AFCON 2027 qualifying campaign as they prepare to face Tanzania in two crucial Group L encounters. item.title: AFCON 2027Q: Guinea-Bissau drop points, hand Super Eagles chance to close gap
item.description: Nigeria’s Super Eagles have received a boost in their quest to qualify for the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations after Guinea-Bissau were held to a 1-1 draw by Madagascar in their Group L encounter on Thursday. The result offers Nigeria an opportunity to reduce the gap at the top of the group following Guinea-Bissau’s impressive start to the qualifying campaign. The Djurtus had taken control of Group L after recording a 3-0 victory over the Super Eagles in their Matchday Two encounter last month. However, they were unable to maintain their winning run against Madagascar, needing a late goal to salvage a point. Warren Caddy gave Madagascar the lead a minute before the hour mark, putting Guinea-Bissau under pressure. But Galatasaray forward Renato Nhaga came to the visitors’ rescue, scoring six minutes from time to secure a 1-1 draw. The result leaves Guinea-Bissau top of Group L with seven points from three matches, while Madagascar sit third with two points. Nigeria can take advantage of the dropped points when they host Tanzania’s Taifa Stars in Uyo on Friday. A victory would strengthen the Super Eagles’ position in the group and provide a much-needed boost to their qualification hopes after their heavy defeat to Guinea-Bissau. The encounter is therefore crucial for Nigeria as they seek to get their AFCON 2027 qualifying campaign back on track. item.title: 2027: Trust me, I won’t fail you, INEC chair assures Nigerians
item.description: By Omeiza Ajayi Chairman of the Independent National Electoral Commission INEC, Prof. Joash Amupitan SAN, has asked Nigerians to trust him to deliver a free, fair, credible and inclusive election next year, promising to not fail them This was as he said the commission is yet to recover from the trust deficit created by the technical glitches associated with the 2023 general election, and vowed that inaccurate polling unit results will not reach the INEC Result Viewing Portal IReV in 2027. Amupitan spoke on Thursday at Chatham House, London, at a dialogue held with the Kimpact Development Initiative (KDI) on the theme, “Nigeria’s 2027 Elections: Democratic Trajectory and Regional Stability Beyond the Ballot.” His Chief Press Secretary, Adedayo Oketola, said the INEC chairman noted that the controversies over the 2023 presidential election badly dented public confidence in the commission. “First, let me speak about what happened in 2023, which resulted in a significant trust deficit for INEC—damage so large that the Commission has not yet fully recovered from it,” he said. He said the commission’s audit after 2023 traced the worst result management failures to collation centres, not polling units. “In 2023, there were instances of inaccurate results or results with over-voting being uploaded onto IReV. We have now devised a technical safeguard: if a result is not accurate at the polling unit, it will not go to IReV at all. The moment a result appears on IReV, citizens can trust what they see. By eliminating inconsistencies at the source, collation will become a transparent formality”, he stated. The INEC chairman announced that the commission would hold a nationwide mock accreditation and voting exercise on November 28, 2026. “On the 28th of this month, we will conduct a mock accreditation and voting exercise across all states of the federation to simulate the presidential election and verify that we have gotten both accreditation and electronic result transmission right,” he said. Asked why Nigerians should trust his leadership, Amupitan who assumed office in October 2025, pointed to the off-cycle elections he had conducted. “Why must Nigerians trust me? Nigerians must trust me because, number one, I have conducted off-cycle elections—and observers agree that the recent election in Osun State marked a clear improvement,” he said. He listed the Anambra and Osun governorship elections, the Federal Capital Territory (FCT) Area Council polls, the Ekiti governorship election and 16 legislative by-elections. Amupitan recalled that the 2021 Anambra governorship poll took roughly five days to conclude, whereas results in Anambra and Osun were declared the day after voting under his watch. “Every election is a lesson. The 2023 general election was a major lesson for Nigeria, and the Anambra election was another,” he said. item.title: Scaloni to stay on as Argentina coach until 2030 World Cup
item.description: Lionel Scaloni on Thursday agreed to stay on as coach of Argentina’s national football team until after the 2030 World Cup, ending the doubts that had been swirling since this year’s World Cup final defeat. Scaloni’s decision to renew his contract was announced by Argentine Football Association president Claudio Tapia at a press conference with the 48-year-old manager. Scaloni, who took the Albiceleste to victory at the 2022 tournament in Qatar, told reporters he was as enthusiastic as “on day one”. “A new project begins now,” he said a month after Lionel Messi, the team’s leading light for 20 years, bowed out of international football. Tapia said that Scaloni would be the Argentina manager with the most World Cups under his belt by the time his contract ended. Scaloni had cast doubt on his future with the team after Argentina’s 1-0 defeat by Spain in a bad-tempered July 19 World Cup final in New Jersey. He has been coach for eight years, taking over in September 2018, after a traumatic World Cup in Russia, where Argentina were eliminated in the round of 16. Scaloni took over one of the most prestigious jobs in football without any prior experience and built the team into one widely considered the best in Argentine history. Besides the 2022 World Cup he coached Argentina to two Copa America titles, in 2021 and 2024. He now faces the task of taking the team forward without his 39-year-old talisman Messi. “What must remain is this team spirit, this feeling of unity among the players and the people,” he said after losing the final to Spain. item.title: Man United closing in on Pochettino after sacking manager Carrick
item.description: United States head coach Mauricio Pochettino is set to be appointed as the new manager of Manchester United after the struggling English giants sacked Michael Carrick on Thursday. Pochettino is expected to leave his role with the USA following their two-legged CONCACAF Nations League quarter-final on Saturday and Tuesday in a move that will see United trigger a release clause worth some $10 million to secure the Argentine’s services. Pochettino, who signed a contract extension to remain with the United States through to the 2030 World Cup just three months ago, is due to hold a pre-match press conference on Friday. Former United captain Carrick led the team to an impressive third-place finish in the Premier League last season, but they have taken just eight points from 10 games in the current campaign and are in the relegation zone. The club confirmed in a statement Thursday that it had parted ways with the 45-year-old, following mounting speculation he would be axed during the international break. “After a disappointing start to the season, the club has come to the extremely difficult conclusion that a change is necessary in order to achieve our ambitions,” United said. “Michael is, and always will be, a Manchester United legend. Just as he did as a player, he has conducted himself with the highest standards of dedication and professionalism throughout his time back with the club.” Carrick impressed after taking over as interim boss following Ruben Amorim’s acrimonious exit in January, leading United to Champions League qualification. He was rewarded with a two-year permanent deal but, hampered by the club’s underwhelming recruitment in the summer transfer window, his side have endured a steep decline this season. Carrick has struggled to maintain discipline, dropping captain Bruno Fernandes after he criticised his manager’s tactics following a 4-1 thrashing at Champions League debutants Como. And defender Lisandro Martinez spoke out against the club’s hierarchy over their lack of top-quality signings. Carrick’s final game in charge was a chaotic 4-4 draw against Aston Villa on Sunday, after which he stressed he would not walk away despite a paltry record of three wins from 15 games in all competitions this season. It is believed Carrick’s future was decided on Wednesday during a meeting in Monaco involving co-owner Jim Ratcliffe, chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox. – ‘Disgusting’ – Pochettino has extensive experience of the Premier League following spells in charge of Southampton, Tottenham and Chelsea, and he also coached Paris Saint-Germain. Carrick, who won multiple trophies as a midfielder in the club’s golden era under Alex Ferguson, is the seventh permanent manager to be dismissed by the club since the Scot retired in 2013. item.title: ‎Nigeria has left ’emergency ward,’ targets $1trn economy by 2030 – Tinubu
item.description: ‎ ‎By Johnbosco Agbakwuru ‎ President Bola Tinubu on Thursday declared that Nigeria’s economy has moved “from stabilisation to shared prosperity,” citing non-oil exports above $6 billion, external reserves of about $55 billion, and a target of a $1 trillion economy by 2030. ‎ ‎Speaking at the public presentation of Economic Diversification and Structural Transformation in Nigeria: Past, Present and Future, authored by Honourable Abdulmumin Jibrin Kofa, Tinubu said the country had abandoned “cosmetic remedies” for what he called the “hard road of surgery.” ‎ ‎According to him: “For too long, Nigeria’s story was a song sung in a single note. We were a nation of boundless promise tied to a single product, our budget, our currency and the livelihoods of millions rising and falling with the tides of a distant oil market. We floated on the fragile illusion of oil wealth while the foundations beneath us crackborders. ‎ ‎”When I took the oath of office, I did not inherit a calm sea; I inherited a gathering storm: a collapsing naira, debt service that swallowed nearly all our revenue, depleted reserves, a fuel subsidy that bled our treasury dry, and factories falling silent as industries and jobs fled across our borders.” ‎ ‎The President said his administration inherited “a gathering storm,” including “a collapsing naira, debt service that swallowed nearly all our revenue, depleted reserves, a fuel subsidy that bled our treasury dry, and factories falling silent.” ‎ ‎“We chose reform over ruin. We removed the fuel subsidy. We unified the exchange rate. These were not easy decisions, and I know the weight they placed on every household. But they were necessary, and today the pain is yielding its promise.” ‎ ‎He stated that non-oil activities now account for about 96 per cent of Gross Domestic Product, while non-oil exports have crossed $6 billion, which he described as the highest in Nigeria’s history. ‎ ‎Tinubu also said external reserves had risen to about $55 billion, representing “more than fourteen months of import cover,” and that non-oil revenue had grown from ₦13.63 trillion in 2023 to ₦16.4 trillion in the first half of 2026. ‎ ‎The President said government alone cannot build a $1 trillion economy, adding that wealth must be created by enterprises that “invest, innovate, manufacture and export.” ‎ ‎“Our duty is to clear the path before them,” he said. “That is why our 2025 budget introduced a first-of-its-kind De-risking Framework to draw in private capital, which we expect to provide 86 per cent of the investment our 2030 goal demands.” ‎ ‎He said the administration was harmonising taxes and ending “the menace of multiple taxation.” ‎“We cannot tax our way into prosperity; we must produce our way there,” Tinubu said. ‎ ‎The President said the administration had “fought for Mambilla,” winning a $3.38 billion arbitration at the International Chamber of Commerce in Paris and freeing “a project held hostage for more than nine years.” ‎He added that

item.title: 2027: Tinubu will lose if he contests against anybody picked on street — Dalung
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye African Democratic Congress (ADC) chieftain Solomon Dalung has expressed confidence that President Bola Tinubu would lose the 2027 election even if his opponent were “anybody picked on the street,” arguing that the President was afraid of facing voters. Speaking on Channels Television’s Politics Today on Thursday, Dalung made the prediction while responding to a question about how the opposition could overcome the APC’s resources amid the current internal leadership and legal crisis in the ADC. He nevertheless insisted the party was ready to challenge Tinubu at the ballot. “Since my experience in politics, like I always say, Nigerians, I was brought into politics at a much tender age. I have never seen a weak president in an election like Bola Ahmed Tinubu. If you drag anybody on the street and put him on a ballot at a contest with Tinubu, he will defeat him,” Dalung said. He claimed Tinubu was apprehensive about the election despite having been in office for four years, and challenged the President and APC to let the contest be decided by voters. “Bola Tinubu is so scared, having been in office for four years, he is so scared of election. And all we are seeing in ADC, let’s meet at the ballot. You claim it was the ballot that brought you to power, let’s meet at the ballot,” he said. Dalung also accused the APC of obstructing opposition parties’ campaign activities, alleging that venues had been closed, hotels taken over and party offices sealed. He compared the situation with the 2014 election period, saying the APC would have been left with few places to campaign if it had faced similar restrictions then. “Nobody will be blamed except Tinubu. Why? Because I mean, in the history of Nigeria, we have seen opposition parties contest election, but we have never seen this type of situation. If the PDP in 2014 were closing venues for rallies and taking over hotels, sealing party offices, the APC would have no place to campaign except the streets,” he said. He argued that moving the opposition onto the streets would not weaken its campaign, claiming those attending its gatherings were genuine supporters rather than people hired to fill rallies. “Now, for Tinubu and his APC to move the opposition on pit, they have lost the election. This is because the people we are having on the street are organic followers. Those are the Nigerians that will vote. They are not rented crowds from all over the federation,” Dalung said. item.title: Reps condemn political violence as thugs attack NDC supporters in Lagos; NDC, APC-PCC fault attack
item.description: By By Henry Umoru, and Gift ChapiOdekina The House of Representatives, the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) and the All Progressives Congress Presidential Campaign Council (APC-PCC) have condemned reported cases of political violence across the country following an attack on NDC supporters during a town hall meeting in Lagos. While the NDC demanded an immediate investigation, arrest and prosecution of those responsible for the attack in Lagos, the APC-PCC also condemned the incident and called on security agencies to apprehend the perpetrators. The Lagos State chapter of the APC equally condemned the reported attack but denied any involvement, challenging the NDC to provide credible evidence linking the ruling party to the incident. The House of Representatives, on Wednesday, also resolved to investigate reported attacks, intimidation and disruption of political activities across the country ahead of the 2027 general elections. The resolution followed the adoption of a motion of urgent public importance sponsored by the House Minority Leader, Rep. Fred Agbedi, and 16 other lawmakers, amid growing concerns over attacks on political meetings, rallies and processions in different parts of the country. Presenting the motion on behalf of the sponsors, Agbedi condemned acts of violence, intimidation, assault and destruction of property associated with political activities, irrespective of the political parties or individuals affected. He appealed to political parties, candidates and their supporters to reject inflammatory rhetoric, discourage violence and cooperate with security agencies to maintain public peace. Citing Section 40 of the 1999 Constitution, as amended, the Minority Leader reminded lawmakers that Nigerians were guaranteed the right to assemble freely and associate with others, including the right to form or belong to political parties. He also cited the constitutional provision which makes the security and welfare of the people the primary purpose of government, stressing the need to protect citizens participating in legitimate political activities. Agbedi urged the House to invoke Section 88(1) of the Constitution, which empowers the National Assembly to investigate matters within its legislative competence and examine the conduct of public authorities responsible for administering relevant laws. To illustrate the growing concerns, he cited several incidents of political violence recorded in different states. He recalled the disruption of political meetings in Enugu State on September 12, 2026, during which the police reportedly confirmed that two attendees were injured, while one person was allegedly killed. He also cited an attack on APC supporters travelling to a rally in Katsina State on October 28, 2026, which led to the arrest of 14 suspects. item.title: Join Rainbow Coalition or leave, Fubara warns supporters
item.description: Rivers State Governor, Siminalayi Fubara, has warned his supporters who are unwilling to align with the Rainbow Coalition to leave, insisting that his decision to return to his political camp is final. Fubara gave the warning on Thursday during the inauguration of the Rivers State All Progressives Congress (APC) Presidential Campaign Council, Rainbow Coalition, in Port Harcourt. Addressing party members and supporters, the governor urged those whose names were not included in the campaign council list not to feel aggrieved, explaining that there were still sub-committees to be constituted and that the list could be updated. He, however, warned against double-dealing, insisting that those claiming to support him must demonstrate genuine commitment to the coalition. “We still have sub-committees. The list can also be updated so you don’t have any problems to worry about. The most important thing is to work with your heart sincerely. “Don’t openly say you’re with me and behold you’re doing a different thing. I’m here, and I say it boldly anywhere, any day. And anybody who says he is not with me, gently go your way,” he said. Acknowledging that some of his supporters might find it difficult to accept the new political direction, Fubara urged them to put the past behind them and embrace the future. “Don’t go behind and say this is Fubara, no, no, no. I have said it. It might be difficult but we have gone past that. We are looking at the future and what God holds for us,” he added. The governor charged members of the campaign council to work together to achieve their political objectives, expressing confidence that the coalition would record more votes in the forthcoming elections than it secured in 2023. “Nothing is impossible. Provided it’s something that has to do with life, it is possible if we take it as a serious responsibility, a serious task that must be achieved, we will come out with a stronger vote than what we did in 2023. “It is only for us to say yes, we want to do it. And I am very sure that with the strategy of these forthcoming elections we are going to come out with good results better than what we had before,” he said. Fubara also thanked the Minister of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Nyesom Wike, and other political leaders for their efforts in establishing the campaign council. Earlier, Wike, who inaugurated the council, announced plans to establish similar campaign structures across the 23 local government areas of Rivers State. He said the coalition would abandon conventional campaign rallies in favour of direct engagement with residents through community gatherings, family meetings and age-grade associations. “We are going away from that ceremonial campaign style. item.title: De Miguel death made me thank God over Zidane headbutt — Materazzi
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Former Italy defender Marco Materazzi says the death of Spanish striker Jesus de Miguel after an on-field collision made him reflect on the headbutt he suffered from Zinedine Zidane in the 2006 World Cup final. Materazzi said the incident, one of football’s most infamous World Cup moments, still troubled him 20 years later. He told Italian newspaper La Gazzetta dello Sport that De Miguel’s death made him grateful he had escaped serious injury. “The death of Jesus de Miguel made me thank God that nothing had happened to me,” Materazzi said in an interview published on Thursday. De Miguel, a Tenerife striker, died after colliding with Andorra goalkeeper Jesus Owono during a Segunda Division match earlier this month. Zidane, then captain of France, was sent off for headbutting Materazzi in the chest during the 2006 final, which Italy won on penalties. Zidane, now France coach, said last month he was not proud of the headbutt but did not regret it. Materazzi said he and Zidane appeared to put the episode behind them when they met before a match in 2010, although Zidane later disputed Materazzi’s account of the encounter. “When he saw me, he hesitated a little, he even turned to walk back,” Materazzi said. “But I approached him and shook his hand: ‘I’m glad we’re meeting here, where nobody can see us.’ “He replied: ‘Don’t worry, these things happen, it’s all in the past.’ It’s a shame he later denied everything, saying he thought I was a fan.” France are scheduled to play Italy in the Nations League later on Thursday. item.title: Tinubu’s economic reforms key to sustainable security, says Dare
item.description: Former Minister of Youth and Sports Development, Sunday Dare, has said President Bola Tinubu’s economic reforms and social interventions constitute an important part of a sustainable national security strategy, arguing that insecurity cannot be tackled through military operations alone. Dare, who disclosed this in a post on his X platform on Thursday, said economic development, effective governance and social inclusion were critical to addressing the underlying conditions that fuel insecurity. He observed that public discussions on national security often focused largely on military interventions, while overlooking the structural impact of economic policies and social programmes on the factors that sustain insecurity. According to him, states with poor developmental indices often record high levels of fragility, reinforcing the need to complement military operations with investments in development and effective governance. Dare cited the security intervention in Birnin Gwari, Kaduna State, as an example of how improved security could support economic recovery and restore livelihoods. He said the intervention by Tinubu had enabled farmers to return to their farms, created employment opportunities for young people and improved productivity. He also credited Kaduna State Governor, Uba Sani, with providing an account of the development and its impact on communities in the area. Highlighting some of the Federal Government’s policies with security implications, Dare identified the Nigerian Education Loan Fund (NELFUND), local government autonomy and increased Federation Account Allocation Committee (FAAC) allocations to states and local governments. On NELFUND, he said expanding access to tertiary education would promote social inclusion and create opportunities for young people who might otherwise be excluded from educational advancement. According to him, providing legitimate pathways to education and economic opportunities could reduce the vulnerability of young people to recruitment by insurgents and other violent groups. He described education not merely as a social investment but also as a long-term investment in national security. On local government autonomy, Dare said adequately resourced and accountable councils could strengthen government presence in communities through improved public services and development initiatives. He argued that responsive governance at the grassroots would reduce the opportunities for violent non-state actors to exploit poorly governed communities and public disaffection. The former minister also said improved FAAC allocations could enhance the capacity of state and local governments to invest in infrastructure, education, healthcare, employment and other essential services. He, however, stressed that such resources must be transparently and productively deployed to address socioeconomic grievances and vulnerabilities that contribute to insecurity. item.title: 2027: Opposition parties lack experience to govern Nigeria, says Ambode
item.description: By Olasunkanmi Akoni Former Lagos State Governor, Akinwunmi Ambode, has criticised opposition parties seeking to unseat the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) in the 2027 general elections, saying they lack the political experience and leadership depth required to govern Nigeria. Ambode specifically mentioned the African Democratic Congress (ADC), the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) and other opposition platforms, arguing that the APC had greater political experience and ideological consistency. He spoke at the APC East Senatorial District rally held at Epe Recreational Ground, Epe, Lagos State, where he canvassed support for President Bola Tinubu, the party’s Lagos governorship candidate, Dr Kadri Obafemi Hamzat, and other APC candidates ahead of the 2027 elections. Ambode said the APC had remained consistent in its political identity, unlike some politicians who, according to him, frequently moved from one political party to another. “APC is our party. We are a collective of the progressives. We have been consistent and delivering for the party. Over the years, we have remained with the progressives and we do not move from one party to another like other people,” he said. Describing the APC as a party connecting the country’s past, present and future, the former governor argued that its political experience placed it in a different position from opposition parties seeking to take over the reins of government. He also credited Tinubu’s political vision and record as Lagos governor with contributing to the state’s economic and infrastructural development, particularly its emergence as a major investment destination. Ambode said the foundations laid during Tinubu’s tenure as governor helped create an environment for financial institutions and corporate organisations to establish and expand their operations in Lagos. “Whether you like him or not, he is a visionary leader. If not for Tinubu, who laid the foundation for the Lagos of today, all the financial firms that have their headquarters in Lagos would have been struggling to survive. But today, his vision has assisted the country to remain an investor destination,” he said. He urged Lagos residents and Nigerians across different social and economic backgrounds to support the APC in the forthcoming elections. Ambode also appealed to members of the Igbo community living in Lagos and other parts of the country to consider national unity and their economic interests when making political choices. “To my Igbo brothers, wherever you live and get your prosperity, that is where you should call home. item.title: Kwara PDP Candidate Kawu Pledges ₦100bn Security Fund
item.description: The governorship candidate of the Peoples Democratic Party in Kwara State, Sulaiman Bolakale Kawu, has pledged to establish a ₦100bn security trust fund and introduce a 13th-month salary for civil servants if elected governor in the 2027 governorship election. Kawu made the pledges in Ilorin during the public presentation of his manifesto, tagged The SBK Compact – Kwara People First, which outlines his proposed policies on security, infrastructure, education, healthcare, agriculture and economic development. The former top civil servant also promised to create 200,000 youth employment opportunities and 5,000 enterprise opportunities annually, alongside a ₦19.2bn agricultural production fund to provide affordable financing and inputs to farmers and cooperatives. He said the proposed ₦100bn security trust fund would finance intelligence-led operations, strengthen community partnerships, equip security agencies and improve coordination among security formations to address insecurity across the state. Kawu said his decision to prioritise security was informed by his visit to Woro community in Kaiama Local Government Area, where he witnessed the aftermath of attacks and the suffering of residents. Sulaiman Bolakale Kawu “One of the most painful experiences in my entire life was my visit to Woro community in Kaiama Local Government Area of our state. I stood before the destruction. I saw blood on the ground. I witnessed firsthand the pain and fear of a traumatised community,” he said. He added that the experience reinforced his determination to ensure that residents could live and conduct their businesses without fear of attacks, kidnapping and other criminal activities. “As Governor, I will not rest or sleep when the life of any Kwaran is under threat,” the PDP candidate said. On workers’ welfare, Kawu promised to introduce a 13th-month salary for all civil servants in the state, assuring that salaries and other entitlements would be paid promptly. “As a retired public servant myself, I understand the sacrifices, expectations and challenges of workers. I will ensure the prompt and timely payment of salaries and other entitlements. Workers must not have to struggle or beg for what they have lawfully earned,” he said. The former civil servant also proposed a ₦9.6bn revolving loan scheme for market traders and another ₦9.6bn single-digit interest loan scheme for micro, small and medium-scale enterprises. He said his administration would establish a ₦3bn Women Enterprises and Empowerment Fund to provide affordable financing and business support to women-owned businesses, while at least 1,000 artisans would receive support grants annually. On grassroots development, Kawu promised to allocate ₦50m to each of the 193 wards in the state within the first 100 days of his administration, amounting to an initial commitment of ₦9.65bn. item.title: I won’t leave England before Euro 2028 —Tuchel
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Thomas Tuchel has ruled out leaving England for a club job before Euro 2028, saying he wants to see out his contract and complete what he calls “unfinished business” with the national team. According to ESPN, Tuchel said there was “no release clause” in his England contract and “no intention” of leaving before the tournament. His comments come amid Manchester United’s move to replace Michael Carrick with Mauricio Pochettino. “I signed a contract; I want to stay until the Euros. I want to do the Euros. We have unfinished business,” Tuchel said. The German succeeded Gareth Southgate in 2025 and signed a two-year extension in February, keeping him in charge through Euro 2028. Tuchel said he was “open for everything” once his contract ends, including staying with England, but confirmed he eventually wants to return to club management. “Yes, definitely,” he said when asked if he would return to club football. “I miss the 50 matches. I miss these two minutes when everything is done.” Tuchel said he also understood the pressures of the club game, where matches come every few days. He said he was grateful for his England role and the freedom to work with his staff. “I’m very grateful for what I have here because I know how rare it is to be in love with your team and to have the trust and to be able to work freely with your coaching staff, which I am,” he said. Tuchel also said he felt aligned with the Football Association from their first discussions and valued the trust of chief executive Mark Bullingham and chief football officer Dan Ashworth. “That’s what you look for as a coach,” he said. “I love my group of players. I love my staff, and I have bosses who trust me and are happy with the way we do things, so it’s a lot. “I appreciate it a lot, so it’s in a good place, I’m in a good place, and I love the players. I miss my players, and I miss my team, and I miss the 50 matches that I’m not involved in a year. “But I’m desperate to win the Nations League and to play and try to win the Euros.” The post I won’t leave England before Euro 2028 —Tuchel appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: PHOTOS: Nigerian High Commissioner, others present Letters of Credence to Ghanaian President
item.description: President John Dramani Mahama of the Republic of Ghana has received Letters of Credence from the 11 newly appointed Ambassadors and High Commissioners. Diplomats from South Africa, Nigeria, India, Thailand, Lebanon, Australia, Switzerland, the Netherlands, Finland, Slovakia and Sweden presented their letters to the President at Jubilee House, Accra. Addressing the diplomatic representatives, President Mahama reaffirmed Ghana’s commitment to deepening diplomatic engagement, strengthening bilateral relations and exploring new areas of mutually beneficial cooperation. He highlighted Ghana’s interest in strengthening its historical, political, cultural and economic ties with partner nations, while calling for greater international collaboration in advancing shared priorities, including Africa’s development, reparatory justice and investment opportunities.
